analyzed_vuln.description: `dissect_softether_host_fqdn` performs length-unsafe string comparisons on parsed VALUE_DATA fields: `strncmp(val1.value.ptr.value_str, "host_name", value_siz)` and `strncmp(val2.value.ptr.value_str, "ddns_fqdn", val2.value_size)`. The third argument comes from attacker-controlled parsed field length, not the literal length or validated buffer bounds. When the parsed field is shorter/non-NUL-terminated or points near poisoned boundary, `strncmp` reads past valid bytes, causing the ASan use-after-poison read seen at line 230.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via `fuzz_process_packet`, attacker-controlled packet bytes are passed directly to `ndpi_detection_process_packet`, which routes to `ndpi_search_softether` for payloads >=99 bytes, then to `dissect_softether_host_fqdn`. Crafting SoftEther-like tuple metadata so `val2.type == VALUE_DATA` and `val2.value_size > 0` but with insufficient backing bytes for comparing against "ddns_fqdn" (or similarly for "host_name") triggers over-read in `strncmp` with attacker-sized length.
